title: Bram and the Clock
premise: In 1916, Theo Fairweather, a hospital clerk and battlefield nurse in a Channel port town, keeps a private ledger of soldiers' names that official reports omit. When a wounded stranger arrives carrying letters in the unmistakable handwriting of Captain Elias Bram — a man officially dead for two years and now declared an enemy collaborator — Theo is forced to choose between the record he trusts and the promise he made to Bram in peacetime: that if ever asked, he would help him come home. As military intelligence closes in and the morning tide approaches, Theo smuggles Bram through occupied wards, forged ledgers, and old loyalties, discovering that the ledger's missing names were Bram's doing all along. At the pier at dawn, Theo must decide whether truth or duty boards the ship; he chooses both, sending Bram away alive while publishing the true names, ending the book with history no longer happening to other people.
about_author: B. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in coastal hospital records. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Theo Fairweather, POV. In a Channel port hospital, Theo records the names officers leave off casualty lists, believing history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet devotion to the forgotten, establishing his moral compass and loneliness.

chapters.title: A Stranger Off the Night Boat
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. A half-drowned man is carried in with no papers and a letter sewn into his coat — addressed to Theo, in handwriting he knows intimately. Emotional beat: shock cracking open Theo's ordered world.

chapters.title: The Hand of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The letter is from Elias Bram, declared dead two years ago, asking Theo to honor their peacetime promise. The stranger, Anselm, whispers only one word before collapsing: 'alive.' Emotional beat: disbelief warring with hope.

chapters.title: What We Promised in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback through Theo's memory. A summer before the war: Bram, then a young officer, and Theo seal a drunken vow — if either ever needs to disappear, the other will make it so. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by dread of what the promise may cost.

chapters.title: The Intelligence Man
chapters.summary: Major Corvane, POV. A cold, meticulous intelligence officer arrives investigating leaked casualty records and a 'ghost' said to be moving along the coast. Emotional beat: menace entering the story; the reader learns the hunt has already begun.

chapters.title: Enemy by Declaration
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo learns Bram is officially listed as a traitor who defected — and that helping him is treason. He hides Anselm in the morgue annex. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Anselm Wakes
chapters.summary: Anselm, POV. The stranger recovers enough to tell his story: he was Bram's batman, and Bram saved him twice. He carries more letters, each naming people on Theo's ledger. Emotional beat: found family beginning to form between strangers bound by one man.

chapters.title: The Missing Forty-Three
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Cross-referencing his ledger with Bram's letters, Theo realizes the 'omitted' names were men Bram secretly evacuated — the ledger and the ghost are the same story. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything Theo believed about cowardice and loyalty.

chapters.title: Corvane Reads the Ward
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. The major interviews staff, charming and precise, and nearly discovers Anselm. Sister Agnes lies for the first time in thirty years. Emotional beat: the net tightening; ordinary people choosing sides.

chapters.title: Sister Agnes's Silence
chapters.summary: Agnes, POV. The matron reflects on the sons she has buried and decides the ledger matters more than her clean record. She gives Theo the keys to the boathouse. Emotional beat: quiet sacrifice; loyalty outweighing obedience.

chapters.title: A Message in the Tide Line
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. A coded note washes up arranged in Bram's style: a rendezvous at the ruined lighthouse, three nights hence, before a ship sails on the morning tide. Emotional beat: urgency igniting; the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Theo and Anselm, alternating. At the lighthouse they find not Bram but his contact, Marta, a smuggler who tests their trust brutally. Emotional beat: tension and doubt — is this rescue or a trap?

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. She reveals Bram is hiding nearby, wounded, but passage costs more than money: Theo must forge discharge papers using real ledger names. Emotional beat: moral compromise; truth becoming currency.

chapters.title: Forging the Living
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo commits forgery, turning his sacred record into a tool of escape, and hates how easily his hand obeys. Emotional beat: guilt and exhilaration entwined; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Salt House
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo finally sees Bram — gaunt, feverish, alive. Their reunion is angry as much as tender: Bram never told him, let him mourn. Emotional beat: love against resentment; the promise renewed under strain.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes In
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. The major finds Anselm's bloodied uniform and deduces the route. He offers Theo immunity in exchange for Bram — revealing he knew Theo's father, and what happened to him. Emotional beat: personal leverage; duty weaponized.

chapters.title: The Father's File
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Corvane shows Theo that his father was erased from the records too — a name in someone else's forgotten ledger. Theo understands why he keeps his own. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into clarity about whose side history is written on.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Anselm, POV. A ward orderly, terrified for his family, tips off Corvane. Soldiers raid the boathouse; Marta is taken covering their escape. Emotional beat: betrayal by the weak, heroism by the unlikely; devastating loss.

chapters.title: Running the Quay
chapters.summary: Theo and Bram, alternating. Through fog and searchlights they carry Anselm toward the ship, Bram too weak to run alone — the rescuer rescued. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; the climax begins.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At the pier, Corvane blocks the gangway. Theo offers a trade: himself and the full ledger in exchange for Bram and Anselm sailing free. Emotional beat: climax — love against duty resolved by refusing the choice itself.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Detained but unbroken, Theo reads the forty-three names aloud at his hearing until the room cannot bear its own silence; public pressure forces Corvane to stand down. Emotional beat: truth as weapon and shield; vindication without victory.

chapters.title: History Happens Here
chapters.summary: Theo, POV, months later. Bram returns when the war shifts, Anselm stays as the hospital's porter, and Theo publishes the ledger complete. On the quay where it began, he watches the morning tide and knows exactly where history happens. Emotional beat: resolution — found family, truth honored, love kept.
